title: Endothelins positively influences the proliferation vs. migration balance of IDH1-mutant glioma cells and promotes proneural to mesenchymal transition
projectDescription: Adult diffuse gliomas are the deadliest brain tumours including IDH-wildtype glioblastomas of worst prognosis and diffuse low grade IDH-mutant astrocytomas and oligodendrogliomas. These glial tumours display distinct tumoral cell population defeating current therapies. Our group has previously unveiled the role of NOTCH signalling in glioblastoma cell plasticity and in the conversion of oligodendrocytic-like to astrocytic-like tumoral cells in IDH-mutant low-grade gliomas which escalate inevitably to higher grade malignant gliomas. To gain insight into signalling pathways regulating glioma cell plasticity and malignancy, we focused our work on endothelin signalling including endothelin peptide ligands (ET-1, ET-2, ET-3) binding to G-protein coupled endothelin receptors A and B (EDNRA, EDNRB). Here, using glioma patient samples and glioma patient-derived cell lines, we showed that endothelin reduces glioma cell proliferation while increasing migration initiating a proneural to mesenchymal transition. Mechanistically, EDNRB activation led to IP3-dependent calcium mobilization, apamin-sensitive KCNN2/KCNN3 potassium currents and phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and STAT3 in glioma cells. Finally, we studied endothelin receptor regulation by tumoral microenvironment stimuli highlighting a role for EDNRA induced by NOTCH1 and hypoxia in perivascular hypoxic area in glioblastoma. Altogether, this study demonstrates endothelin signalling as a key player in mesenchymal transformation of diffuse IDH-mutant gliomas and glioblastomas.
sampleProcessingProtocol: LGG275 cells were dissociated and seeded with 1,5.106 cells in 100 mm Petri dishes (#150350, ThermoFisher Nunclon Delta surface) with 10 mL of medium +GFs per dish. Immediately after cell sedimentation, cells were treated with endothelin dilution buffer (PBS with BSA 0.1%) for the "Vehicle" condition or with ET-1 endothelins at 4 nM final for the "ET-1" condition. This treatment was performed once daily for 5 days before proceeding with protein extraction in RIPA supplemented with protease and phosphatase inhibitors 8 h after the last treatment. Western blot analysis was performed for the 5 independent experiments to assay proteins and ensure quality control (minimum 100 μg protein in 50 μl RIPA). Quality Check included a Western blot against EDNRB, CTGF and OLIG1. Samples were then digested with trypsin (s-TRAP) before proceeding to TMTp10 kit according to manufacturer’s instructions (Thermo Fisher Scientific, batch YA332834). Samples were mixed prior to fractionation (8 fractions) on a basic RP column (Thermo Fisher Scientific, 84868). The 8 fractions were taken up in A buffer (0.1% formic acid) and injected for on-line analysis using a nano flow HPLC (RSLC U3000, Thermo Fisher Scientific) coupled to a mass spectrometer equipped with a FAIMS source (Exploris480, Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were separated on a capillary column (0.075mmx 250mm, Acclaim Pepmap 100, reversed-phase C18, NanoViper, Thermo Fisher Scientific) following a gradient of 2-40% B buffer in 120 min (A=0.1% Formic Acid B=0.1% Formic Acid, 80% Acetonitrile) at a flow rate of 300 nl/min. The spectra were recorded using Xcalibur 4 software (Thermo Fisher Scientific) with the 120minFAIMS_2CV4560_TMT10_ModSU.meth method.
dataProcessingProtocol: Raw FAIMS data was splitted using a ThermoFisher “export Raw file” tool according to CV. The spectral data were analysed using MaxQuant 2.0.3.0 using the FPP v3.5 leading script. The following databases were used: "RefProteome_HUMAN-cano_2023_02_UP000005640.fasta and contaminants_fpp_180320.fasta with the following fixed modification: Carbamidomethylation (C) and the following variable modifications: Oxidation (M), Acetyl (Protein N-term). Data validation was performed with the following filters: 1% FDR at the protein and peptide level for identification.
